questions.corrige_markdown: **Nutrition** is the process by which living organisms obtain food and use it (taking in, digesting, absorbing and assimilating food substances) to get **energy**, to **grow**, to **repair** worn-out tissues and to stay healthy.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write short notes on the following classes of food indicating their chemical composition, basic building units, two functions and an example in each case:

(i) Carbohydrates

(ii) Proteins

(iii) Lipids. *(5, 5, 4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Carbohydrates**

- *Chemical composition:* carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only, with hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2 : 1 as in water.
- *Basic building units:* simple sugars (**monosaccharides**, such as glucose); two sugars make a disaccharide and many make a polysaccharide.
- *Functions:* (1) the main source of **energy** (about 17 kJ per gram); (2) **storage** of energy as starch in plants and glycogen in animals; they also form cellulose in plant cell walls and supply fibre (roughage).
- *Example:* glucose, sucrose or starch (found in yam, cassava, rice, bread).

**(ii) Proteins**

- *Chemical composition:* carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and **nitrogen**, often with sulphur and sometimes phosphorus.
- *Basic building units:* **amino acids**, joined by peptide bonds.
- *Functions:* (1) **growth** and **repair** of tissues (body building); (2) making **enzymes, hormones, antibodies** and haemoglobin; they can also be used as a source of energy when carbohydrates and fats are lacking.
- *Example:* meat, fish, eggs, beans, milk (casein), groundnuts.

**(iii) Lipids (fats and oils)**

- *Chemical composition:* carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, but with much less oxygen than carbohydrates.
- *Basic building units:* **fatty acids and glycerol** (one molecule of glycerol joined to three fatty acids).
- *Functions:* (1) a rich source of **energy** (about 39 kJ per gram, more than twice that of carbohydrates) and a store of energy; (2) **insulation** under the skin to reduce heat loss, and **protection** of organs such as the kidneys; they also dissolve vitamins A, D, E and K and form part of cell membranes.
- *Example:* palm oil, groundnut oil, butter, fat of meat.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name ONE deficiency disease caused by the absence of the following in the diet:

(i) Calcium

(ii) Vitamin A

(iii) Vitamin C

(iv) Proteins. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Missing from the diet | Deficiency disease |
|---|---|
| (i) Calcium | **Rickets** in children (soft, bent bones; with lack of vitamin D) or **osteoporosis** / weak bones and teeth in adults |
| (ii) Vitamin A | **Night blindness** (or xerophthalmia, dry eyes) |
| (iii) Vitamin C | **Scurvy** (bleeding gums, slow healing of wounds) |
| (iv) Proteins | **Kwashiorkor** (swollen belly, thin limbs, oedema) |
